summary: Likely synthetic: the face looks machine-made, and the AI-image detector found generator fingerprints.

tests.name: AI Face Analysis (per-frame)
tests.finding: Face looks synthetic in 100% of 29 sampled frames.
tests.explain: Faces are found in up to 48 frames spread across the clip and the general AI-image detector scores each face crop; averaging many frames is steadier than one still. It catches generated (GAN or diffusion) faces but misses most face-swaps and lip-syncs, which keep a real face's texture.

tests.name: Face-Swap Detector
tests.finding: No face-swap traces found (this test only raises alarms).
tests.explain: Two pretrained deepfake detectors that we benchmarked and chose, not trained ourselves: GenD (a CLIP vision transformer tuned on FaceForensics++, WACV 2026) and the Deepfake Detection Challenge winner (EfficientNet-B7). Each finds the face in 8 frames (GenD also aligns it) and gives the probability that it was swapped or re-animated; such detectors are trained to pick up blending seams and texture mismatches. Thresholds chosen on FaceForensics++ only. It can only raise an alarm: it never vouches that a face is real.

tests.name: AI-Generated Frames
tests.finding: Generator fingerprints in the frames themselves.
tests.explain: The same whole-image AI detector used for photos is run on frames spread across the clip. Fully generated videos and animated AI faces carry generator fingerprints in every frame. It was not trained on face-swaps or lip-sync, and heavy video compression can fool it either way.

tests.name: Blink Rate (Eye Aspect Ratio)
tests.finding: 0 blinks in 12 s (0/min): a little low, short clip.
tests.explain: The Eye Aspect Ratio divides the eye's height by its width using six landmarks; it drops sharply when the eyelid closes. Humans blink about 15-20 times a minute at rest, fewer when reading or concentrating, and modern deepfakes blink normally, so very few blinks is weak evidence and a normal rate proves nothing.

tests.name: Landmark Jitter
tests.finding: Face geometry is frozen (0.02% movement) - like a moving photograph.
tests.explain: We track 478 facial landmarks about 12 times a second, cancel out normal head movement with a similarity transform, and measure how much the remaining points shake. Bone does not wobble, so strong jitter points to frame-by-frame synthesis - while zero movement means a still photo is being animated.

tests.name: Temporal Flicker
tests.finding: Face and background light change together (0.2x ratio) - natural.
tests.explain: We record the average brightness and colour of the face and of the background in every frame, remove slow changes, and compare the fast flicker. Real lighting affects both together; a face synthesised frame by frame flickers on its own, giving a high face-to-background flicker ratio.

tests.name: Metadata & Provenance
tests.finding: Re-encoded with FFmpeg; original device tags are gone.
tests.explain: Video files carry container tags: phones record make, model and creation time, editors and converters stamp their encoder name, and some AI video tools add their own name or a C2PA content credential. Tags are easy to strip, so they are supporting evidence only.
